verdict.rationale: GrowthBook ships its own environments feature (dev, staging, production), so flags can be enabled or toggled per environment, including via API. A self-hosted local instance was also verified in a keyless runtime probe, which gives a separate place to test. However, environments separate flag state rather than offering a documented, data-isolated sandbox, and custom environments are listed under a higher pricing tier. missing for 10: explicit documentation that non-production environments are isolated from production data, a dedicated sandbox or test-mode org, guidance for agents/MCP to target a sandbox environment, independent hands-on corroboration of environment isolation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Use environments such as dev, staging, and production to enable or disable feature flags independently.
Feature flags can be enabled and disabled on a per-environment basis.
automate it (for example, from a deploy script) with the toggle feature endpoint, which switches a flag on or off in one or more environments.
